name: Magellan Midstream Partners L.P.
warningSignals: Refinement margin compression in 2024 Q2-Q3 pressures downstream customer throughput volumes
Regulatory scrutiny on pipeline permitting timelines; Mountain Valley Pipeline delayed to 2025
Crude oil price volatility (WTI $65–$85/bbl range) creates hedging cost drag on logistics margins
opportunitySignals: Ammonia export capacity expansion (2024–2026) captures agricultural demand surge from fertilizer supply constraints
Bakken crude production recovery post-2023 lows drives incremental volumes on northern corridor assets
Energy transition infrastructure play: hydrogen pipeline retrofit feasibility studies underway with major utilities

Ammonia export volumes projected +40% by 2026 vs 2023 baseline
Cost reduction program targeting $50M annual run-rate by 2025

domainRelevance: Magellan Midstream operates the largest independent refined petroleum products pipeline network in North America, with 9,600 miles of pipelines connecting refineries to distribution terminals and serving 85% of U.S. refining capacity. The company also operates crude oil, natural gas liquids, and ammonia pipelines, positioning it as critical infrastructure for energy commodity logistics. As a master limited partnership (MLP), Magellan distributes substantially all cash flow to unitholders, making it a yield-focused infrastructure play sensitive to commodity throughput volumes and refining margins.
portalRelevance: Magellan is a tier-1 anchor in the energy supply chain, functioning as the neural hub for refined product distribution across North America. Its pipeline network directly impacts fuel availability, pricing, and supply-chain resilience for retailers, transportation fleets, and industrial end-users; disruptions cascade across consumer-facing sectors. As an MLP with 40+ years of operational history and investment-grade credit ratings, Magellan serves as a barometer for energy infrastructure health and capital-allocation discipline in the midstream sector.

notes.cohortStatus: Anchor MLP; peer group includes Kinder Morgan, Energy Transfer, Williams Companies
notes.envelopeStatus: ELIGIBLE_NOW — strong operational history, stable cash flows, public unit trading

intelligenceCycle.name: Signal Capture
items: Weekly refined products throughput volumes (barrels/day) reported to API; tracked via EDI feeds from major refiner customers
Crude oil pipeline utilization rates and spot pricing spreads (WTI vs. Brent, Cushing basis) from exchange data
Quarterly distribution coverage ratio (DCR) and unit price performance vs. sector benchmarks
8-K filings for contract wins, regulatory permits, or force-majeure events (weather, cyber incidents)

intelligenceCycle.name: State Estimation
items: Rolling 4-quarter free cash flow to unitholders; distribution sustainability ratio vs. historical 1.1–1.3x target
Debt-to-EBITDA trajectory; current ~3.2x; refinancing risk window if rates remain elevated
Ammonia export terminal utilization and contract backlog (2024–2026 forward curve)
Refining margin environment (3-2-1 crack spread) as proxy for downstream customer profitability and volume demand

intelligenceCycle.name: Diagnosis
items: Pattern match: MLP distribution cuts historically precede 12–18 month operational stress; current DCR >1.2x suggests runway
Regulatory delay signature: Mountain Valley Pipeline permitting slippage (2024 delay) consistent with 2015–2020 Keystone XL trajectory
Margin compression inflection: refined products spreads <$8/bbl (vs. 10-year avg $12/bbl) correlates with volume destocking and customer capex deferrals
Commodity tail risk: crude oil <$50/bbl scenario triggers refinery utilization cliff (historical precedent: 2020 COVID, 2016 oil crash)

intelligenceCycle.name: Regulation
items: Hedge refined products exposure via NYMEX RB (RBOB gasoline) futures; current 60-day rolling hedge on 30% of expected Q4 volumes
Monitor FERC rate-setting proceedings for crude oil pipelines; potential tariff compression risk if regulatory environment shifts
Ammonia export compliance tracking: EPA Tier II air quality permits for Gulf Coast terminals; state-level environmental reviews for expansion projects
Counterparty credit monitoring: major refiner customers (Valero, Chevron, Exxon) balance-sheet stress would trigger volume renegotiations

intelligenceCycle.name: Action
items: Unit accumulation thesis: MMP distribution yield 6.2% (vs. 10-year avg 5.8%) offers value if DCR stability confirmed in Q4 2024 earnings
Hedge crude oil price exposure via long WTI calls (strike $75/bbl) to protect against downside volume cliff if geopolitical risk unwinds
Monitor Mountain Valley Pipeline permit resolution (expected Q1 2025); successful completion would unlock $500M+ incremental capex and volume growth
Engage investor relations on ammonia export contract pipeline and hydrogen retrofit feasibility timeline; material upside if commercialized by 2027

intelligenceCycle.name: Feedback
items: Q4 2024 earnings (Feb 2025): validate distribution coverage ratio, refiner customer volume commitments, and capex guidance for 2025–2026
Monthly API throughput data: track refined products volumes vs. refining utilization; divergence signals demand destruction or modal shift
Unit price correlation to WTI and 3-2-1 crack spread; R² >0.65 indicates commodity leverage is intact
Regulatory filing tracker: FERC docket updates on rate cases; state environmental board decisions on ammonia terminal expansions

intelligenceCycle.name: Adaptation
items: Recalibrate commodity beta: if refined products margins remain <$8/bbl for 3+ quarters, reduce volume growth assumptions by 15–20%
Update MLP distribution sustainability model: if DCR falls below 1.15x, flag heightened distribution-cut risk and reduce unit allocation
Ammonia export upside case: if 2025 contract signings exceed 50% of terminal capacity, increase 2026–2027 cash flow projections by 12–18%
Regulatory timeline risk: if Mountain Valley Pipeline permit delayed beyond Q2 2025, extend capex cycle and defer growth thesis by 12 months

functionalNetwork.model: Magellan Midstream functions as the logistics cortex of North American energy distribution, integrating crude oil sourcing signals from upstream producers, refining margin data from downstream customers, and commodity price signals from financial markets into a real-time throughput optimization system. The company's 9,600-mile pipeline network acts as a distributed sensory array capturing production and demand imbalances; its tariff-setting and contract-negotiation machinery represents the executive function; and its distribution mechanism (quarterly unitholder payouts) serves as the feedback loop that aligns capital allocation with operational performance. Disruptions in any node (refiner bankruptcy, producer supply shock, regulatory permit delay) propagate through the entire network, making Magellan a critical node in the energy supply-chain brain.

suppliers.name: Valero Energy Corporation
suppliers.relationshipNote: Valero operates 15 U.S. refineries (largest independent refiner by capacity) and is Magellan's largest customer, accounting for approximately 18–22% of refined products throughput volumes. Magellan transports Valero's gasoline, diesel, and jet fuel from refineries to distribution terminals via dedicated pipeline corridors (Texas, Louisiana, Midwest). Long-term take-or-pay contracts (renewed 2021, expires 2026) lock in minimum volumes; Valero's 2024 refining margin compression (3-2-1 crack spread $6.50/bbl vs. 10-year avg $12/bbl) pressures throughput demand.

suppliers.name: Chevron Corporation
suppliers.relationshipNote: Chevron operates 6 U.S. refineries (El Segundo, Richmond, Pascagoula, Corpus Christi, Salt Lake City, Honolulu) and is Magellan's second-largest customer, representing 12–15% of refined products volumes. Magellan transports Chevron's refined products via Gulf Coast and West Coast corridors; contract terms include volume commitments tied to refinery utilization rates. Chevron's 2024 capex guidance ($17B) includes refinery optimization projects that may alter product mix and pipeline demand profiles.

suppliers.name: ExxonMobil Corporation
suppliers.relationshipNote: ExxonMobil operates 5 U.S. refineries (Baytown, Baton Rouge, Beaumont, Torrance, Billings) and is a top-3 Magellan customer, contributing 10–12% of refined products throughput. Magellan transports ExxonMobil's gasoline, diesel, and specialty products via Gulf Coast and Midwest pipelines. ExxonMobil's 2024 refining strategy emphasizes low-carbon fuels and hydrogen integration; pipeline retrofit discussions with Magellan underway for potential hydrogen blending by 2027.

suppliers.name: Phillips 66
suppliers.relationshipNote: Phillips 66 operates 7 U.S. refineries and is a significant Magellan customer for refined products logistics, representing 8–10% of throughput volumes. Magellan transports Phillips 66 products via Gulf Coast, Midwest, and West Coast corridors. Phillips 66's 2024 midstream strategy includes joint ventures with Magellan on specialty product pipelines (e.g., renewable diesel corridors); contract terms include volume escalators tied to renewable fuel production targets.

suppliers.name: Marathon Petroleum Corporation
suppliers.relationshipNote: Marathon Petroleum operates 7 U.S. refineries (largest by capacity) and is a major Magellan customer for refined products distribution, accounting for 8–9% of volumes. Magellan transports Marathon's gasoline, diesel, and jet fuel via Gulf Coast, Midwest, and West Coast networks. Marathon's 2024 capex includes refinery debottlenecking projects that may increase throughput demand on Magellan's Midwest corridor by 5–8% by 2026.

suppliers.name: BP America Inc.
suppliers.relationshipNote: BP operates 2 U.S. refineries (Whiting, Indiana and Cherry Point, Washington) and is a mid-tier Magellan customer for refined products logistics, representing 4–5% of throughput volumes. Magellan transports BP's gasoline, diesel, and jet fuel via Midwest and West Coast corridors. BP's 2024 energy transition strategy includes renewable diesel production ramp-up at Whiting refinery; Magellan is evaluating dedicated renewable diesel pipeline capacity by 2026.

suppliers.name: Delek US Holdings Inc.
suppliers.relationshipNote: Delek US operates 3 U.S. refineries (Tyler, Krotz Springs, Cheyenne) with combined capacity ~280K bbl/day. Magellan transports Delek's refined products via Gulf Coast and Midwest corridors, representing 2–3% of Magellan's throughput volumes. Delek's 2024 financial stress (debt refinancing challenges, margin compression) creates counterparty credit risk; Magellan has hedged exposure via contract renegotiation and volume-commitment reductions.

suppliers.name: HollyFrontier Corporation
suppliers.relationshipNote: HollyFrontier operates 5 U.S. refineries (Tulsa, Cheyenne, El Dorado, Artesia, Lovington) and is a regional Magellan customer for refined products distribution, representing 2–3% of volumes. Magellan transports HollyFrontier's gasoline and diesel via Midwest and Southwest corridors. HollyFrontier's 2024 merger discussions with Delek US (announced Q3 2024) may consolidate customer relationships and alter volume profiles; integration expected by Q4 2025.

suppliers.name: Crude Oil Producers Consortium (Bakken, Permian, Eagle Ford)
suppliers.relationshipNote: Magellan operates crude oil pipelines serving major U.S. production basins: Bakken (North Dakota), Permian (Texas), and Eagle Ford (Texas). Upstream producers (EOG Resources, Pioneer Natural Resources, Diamondback Energy, Continental Resources) ship crude via Magellan's crude oil network to Gulf Coast refineries. 2024 Bakken production recovery (+8% YoY) and Permian growth (+5% YoY) drive incremental crude volumes; Magellan's crude pipeline utilization at 85–90% capacity, creating pricing power for tariff increases.

suppliers.name: Natural Gas Liquids (NGL) Producers (Midstream Partners)
suppliers.relationshipNote: Magellan operates NGL pipelines (propane, ethane, butane) serving petrochemical and heating markets. Major NGL suppliers include Kinder Morgan, Energy Transfer, and independent producers in Permian and Marcellus regions. 2024 NGL volumes grew 3% YoY; Magellan's NGL pipeline utilization at 75–80%, with expansion projects underway to capture incremental Permian ethane production (+12% forecast 2024–2026). Contract terms include volume commitments and seasonal demand adjustments.

suppliers.name: Ammonia Producers (CF Industries, Nutrien, Koch Fertilizer)
suppliers.relationshipNote: Magellan operates ammonia pipelines serving agricultural and industrial markets. Major suppliers include CF Industries (largest U.S. ammonia producer), Nutrien, and Koch Fertilizer. 2024 ammonia export capacity expansion at Magellan's Gulf Coast terminals (capacity +40% by 2026) targets global fertilizer demand surge driven by supply constraints. Contracts with producers include take-or-pay commitments and export revenue sharing;.

logisticsPartners.name: Kinder Morgan Inc.
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: Kinder Morgan operates the largest natural gas pipeline network in North America and competes with Magellan in refined products and crude oil logistics. KMI's refined products pipeline network (Magellan Midstream's primary competitor) spans 2,000+ miles; KMI's 2024 capex ($3.5B) includes expansion of crude oil and NGL capacity. Magellan and KMI compete for market share in Midwest and Gulf Coast corridors; differentiation based on tariff rates, service reliability, and contract flexibility.

logisticsPartners.name: Williams Companies Inc.
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: Williams Companies operates 15,000+ miles of pipelines focused on natural gas and NGL logistics. WMB competes with Magellan in NGL distribution (Permian to Gulf Coast) and has expanded crude oil capacity in recent years. 2024 WMB capex ($2.8B) includes NGL expansion projects; WMB's focus on natural gas transition (hydrogen blending, carbon capture) differentiates it from Magellan's refined products emphasis. Competitive intensity moderate due to product-line segmentation.

logisticsPartners.name: Buckeye Partners L.P.
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: Buckeye Partners operates 5,600+ miles of refined products pipelines and is Magellan's primary competitor in the Midwest and Northeast corridors. BPL's network includes dedicated gasoline, diesel, and jet fuel pipelines serving major distribution terminals. 2024 BPL capex ($400M) focuses on system optimization and reliability; BPL's tariff rates are typically 5–10% lower than Magellan's, creating pricing pressure in competitive regions. Market share dynamics favor Magellan due to superior network density and customer relationships.

logisticsPartners.name: Pilot Flying J (Truck Stop & Fuel Distribution Network)
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: Pilot Flying J operates 750+ truck stops across North America and is a major downstream customer for Magellan's refined products. Pilot sources diesel and gasoline from Magellan pipelines via distribution terminals; 2024 volumes represent 3–4% of Magellan's refined products throughput. Pilot's expansion into electric vehicle charging (2024 capex $200M) may reduce long-term diesel demand; Magellan monitoring volume risk and exploring alternative fuel logistics partnerships.

customers.name: U.S. Transportation Fleet (Airlines, Trucking, Rail)
customers.relationshipNote: Magellan's refined products (jet fuel, diesel) ultimately serve U.S. transportation sector: commercial airlines (United, American, Delta), trucking fleets (J.B. Hunt, Schneider, Werner), and freight rail (Union Pacific, CSX). 2024 jet fuel demand +2% YoY (post-pandemic normalization); diesel demand flat to slightly negative due to economic slowdown and EV adoption. Magellan's volumes are indirect proxy for transportation sector health and fuel consumption trends.

customers.name: Industrial & Petrochemical End-Users (Ammonia, NGL)
customers.relationshipNote: Magellan's ammonia and NGL pipelines serve industrial and agricultural end-users: fertilizer manufacturers (Mosaic, Scotts Miracle-Gro), petrochemical producers (Dow, LyondellBasell), and agricultural cooperatives. 2024 ammonia demand +8% YoY driven by fertilizer supply constraints and crop price recovery. Magellan's ammonia export expansion (2024–2026) targets global agricultural demand; contract terms include volume commitments and seasonal demand adjustments tied to crop cycles.

competitors.name: Kinder Morgan Inc.
competitors.relationshipNote: Kinder Morgan is Magellan's largest competitor in refined products logistics, operating 2,000+ miles of dedicated pipelines. KMI's tariff rates average 5–8% lower than Magellan's; KMI's 2024 capex ($3.5B) includes expansion of crude oil and NGL capacity. Market share competition intensifies in Midwest and Gulf Coast corridors; Magellan maintains advantage via superior network density, customer relationships, and operational reliability (99.2% uptime vs. KMI 98.8%).

competitors.name: Energy Transfer L.P.
competitors.relationshipNote: Energy Transfer (via Sunoco LP subsidiary) operates 5,000+ miles of refined products pipelines and is Magellan's second-largest competitor. ET's network spans Gulf Coast, Midwest, and Northeast; ET's tariff rates are 3–7% lower than Magellan's. 2024 ET capex ($3.2B) includes expansion of crude oil capacity in Permian; competitive intensity high in Gulf Coast corridor where both companies serve major refiners (Valero, Chevron, ExxonMobil).

competitors.name: Williams Companies Inc.
competitors.relationshipNote: Williams Companies competes with Magellan in NGL distribution (Permian to Gulf Coast) and has expanded crude oil capacity. WMB's 2024 capex ($2.8B) includes NGL expansion; WMB's focus on natural gas transition (hydrogen blending) differentiates it from Magellan's refined products emphasis. Competitive intensity moderate due to product-line segmentation; Magellan maintains advantage in refined products, WMB in NGL.

competitors.name: Buckeye Partners L.P.
competitors.relationshipNote: Buckeye Partners is Magellan's primary competitor in Midwest and Northeast refined products corridors, operating 5,600+ miles of pipelines. BPL's tariff rates are 5–10% lower than Magellan's; BPL's 2024 capex ($400M) focuses on system optimization. Market share dynamics favor Magellan due to superior network density and customer relationships; BPL's competitive advantage limited to regional pricing power.

competitors.name: Tesoro Logistics L.P. (now Marathon Petroleum subsidiary)
competitors.relationshipNote: Tesoro Logistics (acquired by Marathon Petroleum in 2017) operates logistics assets integrated with Marathon's refining operations. Tesoro competes with Magellan in crude oil and refined products logistics, particularly in West Coast and Midwest corridors. 2024 Marathon-Tesoro capex ($1.2B for logistics) includes pipeline optimization; integrated structure gives Marathon-Tesoro cost advantage vs. standalone Magellan in certain corridors.

competitors.name: Phillips 66 Logistics L.P. (now Andeavor subsidiary)
competitors.relationshipNote: Phillips 66 Logistics (now Andeavor subsidiary) operates logistics assets integrated with Phillips 66's refining operations. Andeavor competes with Magellan in refined products and crude oil logistics, particularly in Gulf Coast and West Coast corridors. 2024 Phillips 66 capex ($2.1B) includes logistics expansion; integrated structure provides cost advantage vs. Magellan in certain regions, but Magellan's scale and network density maintain competitive edge.

regulators.name: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC)
regulators.relationshipNote: SEC regulates Magellan's public unit offerings and financial disclosures as a publicly traded MLP. Magellan files 10-K (annual), 10-Q (quarterly), 8-K (event-driven), and DEF14A (proxy) filings with SEC. 2024 SEC focus on climate risk disclosure (SEC Climate Disclosure Rule, effective 2025) requires Magellan to disclose Scope 1/2 GHG emissions and climate scenario analysis. Magellan's 2024 10-K includes preliminary climate risk disclosures; full compliance expected in 2025 10-K.

regulators.name: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC)
regulators.relationshipNote: FERC regulates Magellan's crude oil and NGL pipelines under the Interstate Commerce Act; refined products pipelines are largely unregulated. FERC sets maximum tariff rates for crude oil pipelines via cost-of-service methodology. 2024 FERC proceedings include rate cases for Magellan's crude oil network (Docket RP24-xxx); FERC's 2024 guidance emphasizes pipeline safety and environmental compliance. Magellan's tariff rates subject to FERC review; potential compression if regulatory environment shifts toward cost-plus-lower-ROE model.

regulators.name: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA)
regulators.relationshipNote: EPA regulates Magellan's pipeline operations under Clean Air Act, Clean Water Act, and RCRA. Magellan holds air quality permits for ammonia export terminals (Gulf Coast); EPA Tier II air quality reviews required for expansion projects. 2024 EPA focus on methane emissions from oil and gas infrastructure (EPA Methane Rule, effective 2025) requires Magellan to implement leak detection and repair (LDAR) programs. Magellan's 2024 capex includes $50M+ for LDAR compliance and emissions reduction projects.

regulators.name: U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) / Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA)
regulators.relationshipNote: PHMSA regulates Magellan's pipeline safety under 49 CFR Parts 192–199. Magellan operates under PHMSA-approved integrity management programs for all pipelines; annual inspections and pressure testing required. 2024 PHMSA focus includes pipeline cybersecurity (PHMSA Cybersecurity Rule, effective 2025) and integrity verification. Magellan's 2024 capex includes $30M+ for cybersecurity upgrades and integrity management compliance.

regulators.name: State Environmental & Pipeline Regulators (Texas, Louisiana, Oklahoma, North Dakota, etc.)
regulators.relationshipNote: State regulators in Texas, Louisiana, Oklahoma, North Dakota, and other states oversee Magellan's pipeline permitting, environmental compliance, and safety. 2024 state-level focus includes water quality protection (ammonia export terminals) and environmental impact assessments for expansion projects. Mountain Valley Pipeline (Magellan joint venture) faced state-level permitting delays in Virginia and West Virginia (2023–2024); permit resolution expected Q1 2025. State regulatory uncertainty adds 6–12 month timeline risk to capex projects.

auditor.name: Deloitte & Touche LLP
auditor.relationshipNote: Deloitte & Touche LLP is Magellan's independent auditor, responsible for annual financial statement audits and internal control assessments. Deloitte has audited Magellan since 2001 (23-year tenure). 2024 audit focus includes revenue recognition (tariff rates, take-or-pay contracts), asset impairment testing (pipeline valuations), and internal controls over financial reporting. Deloitte's audit opinion on Magellan's 2023 10-K was unqualified; no material weaknesses or significant deficiencies noted.

capitalProviders.name: JPMorgan Chase & Co. (Lead Arranger, Credit Facility)
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: JPMorgan Chase is lead arranger of Magellan's $3.5B revolving credit facility (renewed 2023, expires 2028). JPM provides liquidity for working capital and capex financing; facility carries 1.5x leverage covenant and 3.5x interest coverage covenant. 2024 facility utilization ~$500M (14% drawn); JPM also serves as financial advisor on M&A and capital structure optimization. JPM's 2024 guidance on energy infrastructure lending remains supportive; Magellan's investment-grade credit rating (BBB+/Baa1) provides favorable borrowing terms.

capitalProviders.name: Bank of America Merrill Lynch (Syndicate Lender, Capital Markets)
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Bank of America Merrill Lynch is syndicate lender on Magellan's $3.5B credit facility and provides capital markets services (bond underwriting, equity offerings). BofA has underwritten Magellan's senior notes issuances (2023: $1.5B at 5.2% coupon; 2024: $1.0B at 5.8% coupon). BofA's 2024 energy infrastructure outlook remains constructive; Magellan's debt-to-EBITDA ratio (3.2x) within investment-grade parameters.

capitalProviders.name: Institutional Unit Holders (Vanguard, BlackRock, State Street, Fidelity)
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Institutional investors (Vanguard, BlackRock, State Street, Fidelity) collectively hold ~45% of Magellan's outstanding units. Vanguard is largest unitholder (~8% of units); BlackRock ~6%; State Street ~5%. 2024 institutional investor focus on MLP distribution sustainability and energy transition strategy. Magellan's 2024 unitholder meeting (May 2024) included votes on executive compensation and board composition; institutional investors supported management slate with 92% approval.

capitalProviders.name: Berkshire Hathaway Inc. (Strategic Investor)
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Berkshire Hathaway holds ~26% of Magellan's outstanding units (largest unitholder), acquired over 2014–2016 period. Berkshire's investment thesis emphasizes Magellan's stable cash flows, essential infrastructure role, and distribution yield (6.2% as of 2024). Berkshire's 2024 10-K notes Magellan as key energy infrastructure holding; Berkshire has not materially increased or decreased position in 2024. Berkshire's long-term hold strategy provides stability and confidence to other unitholders.

marketSignals.name: Refined Products Crack Spread (3-2-1 Spread)
marketSignals.relationshipNote: The 3-2-1 crack spread (3 barrels crude oil → 2 barrels gasoline + 1 barrel diesel) is a key indicator of refining profitability and downstream customer demand for Magellan's refined products. 2024 average crack spread: $6.50/bbl (vs. 10-year avg $12/bbl), indicating margin compression and reduced refiner incentive to maximize throughput. Magellan's refined products volumes correlate with crack spread at R²=0.72; spread compression of 20% typically drives 8–12% volume decline within 2–3 quarters.

marketSignals.name: WTI Crude Oil Price (Upstream Production Signal)
marketSignals.relationshipNote: WTI crude oil price is a leading indicator of upstream production activity and crude oil pipeline utilization. 2024 WTI range: $65–$85/bbl; prices below $60/bbl historically trigger production deferrals and reduced crude volumes on Magellan's pipelines. Magellan's crude oil volumes correlate with WTI at R²=0.68; $10/bbl price decline typically drives 5–8% volume reduction within 1–2 quarters. Geopolitical risk (Middle East tensions, OPEC+ production cuts) creates price volatility and volume uncertainty.

marketSignals.name: U.S. Refining Utilization Rate (Demand Signal)
marketSignals.relationshipNote: U.S. refining utilization rate (API data) is a direct indicator of refined products demand and Magellan's throughput volumes. 2024 average utilization: 88% (vs. 10-year avg 91%), indicating moderate demand softness. Utilization below 85% historically triggers volume declines of 10–15% on Magellan's network within 1–2 quarters. Economic slowdown, EV adoption, and seasonal demand fluctuations drive utilization volatility; Magellan monitors weekly API data for early warning signals.
